title: How to organize the pantry bulk storage
description:
Holds the reserve that feeds the working shelves, and nothing else.

This is The Backstock and Bulk in the Pantry. About 45-75 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Sacks of rice, cases of tinned tomatoes and packs of kitchen roll, each written on with the month it arrived, all standing at or below waist height. A maximum number written on the shelf edge for each line, and the count on the shelf sitting at or under it. Nothing stacked in front of anything else.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Open up the back of this zone and meet what you forgot you owned: the second sack of rice, the twelve-pack of a sauce nobody liked, the case of sparkling water from a party in another season.
Straighten: Weight decides height.
Shine: Sweep the floor of this zone and check the underside of the bottom case for damp, where a concrete floor or an outside wall is sweating.
Safety: Fall, cut, or crush: a stacked column of cases is stable right up until somebody pulls the second one from the bottom.
Standardize: Write a maximum for each line on the shelf edge, two of this, one of that, and mark every pack with its arrival month as it goes in.
Sustain: The gap is the signal and the trip is the trigger.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
Every pack carries its arrival month, every line has a maximum written on the shelf edge, and stock is always pulled from the front.
